I'm about to buy my wife a Ruger LC9 for concealed carry. Any ups and downs?

For a 9mm pocket pistol not really. Has she shot pistols before? Larger pistols shoot better, so if she is willing and able to carry anything larger I would suggest that.

Lc9 is 6" x 4.5" x .9" 17.2oz

Sig sauer 1911 ultra 6.8 x 4.8 x 1.4 28 oz

Sigs are expensive but other makers will have the same size. Citadel should be about he same price. That is same capacity but 45. Acp. It will hit harder and be tamer to shoot. Downside is a little larger and heavier.

I agree with Gnawzzy, Ziekk, thedirtypuma, and 1moar on the amount of kick from a 9mm, and checking out the .380 option is well advised. The idea is to become comfortable and familiar with your gun. If it has too much kick, she isn't going to want to practice with it. You want your shared range-time to be fun for both of you.

How familiar with handguns is your wife? The semi-automatic can be difficult to operate when in a panic. Have you considered a snub-nosed revolver, like the Ruger LCR? Point and shoot.

I'm not a fan of .22 caliber for self-defense, but you should consider this as well. If its a more comfortable gun for the shooter, it is the superior self-defense choice.
